info.title: Fenders management API
info.description: The workspace API, which a workspace's key is given, and the operator's routes, which no key is. Deployment/start never invokes a command. Same-key retries return the original operation; command outcomes are observed separately. A key is issued, listed and revoked with the operator credential (/workspaces/{workspace}/api-keys), never with a key; it may carry a label, which GET /me returns and the audit trail records. A change that answers with an operation is 202 while the operation is pending and 200 or 201 once it is not; nothing else is ever 202. HEAD is answered wherever GET is. A route asked with a method it does not take is 405 with Allow. Every list answers {items, next}, newest first, and takes limit (1 to 100) and before; a run's output alone is read forwards, with after. A change names the revision it was decided on as expected_revision, and is 409 revision_conflict if the thing has changed since: an app's revision for the app, its versions, releases, connections and deletion; the triggers' own for the triggers; a workspace's lifecycle_revision and allowance_revision for the operator's changes to it.

get.description: Required permission: read. One timeline, newest first: each HTTP, manual or scheduled invocation is one entry (entry=run, as in List runs) interleaved with recorded lifecycle changes (entry=lifecycle). Command admission and execution transitions are summarized by their invocation unless type=lifecycle or a release, run or execution filter is set; those filters list recorded transitions only. Lifecycle changes and HTTP requests are retained for 30 days.

post.summary: Send one request to an HTTP app
post.description: Makes one request of the app through the gateway, as a client of its URL would, and reports what came back. It is admitted, counted and charged as any request of the app is. The answer is 200 whatever the app or the gateway said; read outcome. Required permission: runs:write.

200.description: The control plane can serve.

apiKey.description: Workspace API key. Permissions and optional project scope are enforced on every request. The operator credential is accepted wherever a key is.

operator.description: The operator credential, written to STATE/operator.token at first start. Not scoped: it may call every route, a workspace's among them.

SubmissionKey.name: key
SubmissionKey.description: The Idempotency-Key the request was made with, percent-encoded as a path segment: a key with a slash or a space in it is found as %2F and %20.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Persist this value for retries of the same intent. Different arguments with the same key return 409.

PageLimit.name: limit
PageLimit.description: How many to answer with at most.

PageBefore.name: before
PageBefore.description: The next of the page before, to continue after it. Pass back what was given: a cursor is not made up.

RequestId.description: This request's id, which a refusal's body carries too. Quote it when asking after a request.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before asking again.

WwwAuthenticate.description: Bearer: a bearer credential is wanted.

Refused.description: The request was refused or could not be served. Error.code says why. 400 for a malformed request, 403 for a credential that may not, 404 for what does not exist or is another workspace's, 409 for a conflict with what is, 413 and 415 for a body too large or not of the type the route takes, 5xx when the control plane could not serve it.

Unauthorized.description: No credential, or one that is revoked, expired or unknown.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path is a route and does not take this method. Any path may answer this; it is not listed with each.

RateLimited.description: Too many changes by this workspace's credentials in a minute, or too much in progress at once. An allowance or a limit reached is 409 quota_exhausted, not this.

error.description: For a person to read. Its wording may change; branch on code.

code.description: Why the request was refused, for a program to branch on. Either the status named, or a reason more specific than it. Codes may be added.

Operation.description: A change that was asked for, and how it stands: nothing of the request that asked it. state is pending until it is made; then succeeded, or failed with error. resource_id is what it changes or makes: an app, a version, a release, a run, a connection.

kind.description: What was asked: deploy-app, create-app, attach-app-version, activate-app-release, run-app, cancel-run, app-lifecycle, app-triggers, app-connections, delete-app, create-external-endpoint, remove-external-endpoint. Kinds may be added.

concurrency.description: Requests one HTTP execution serves at once; each has the size's linear memory, so they must fit it together.

websocket.description: Accept WebSocket connections at the app's URL. Fenders holds each connection and sends the app its events as POST requests to /_fenders/ws/connect, /_fenders/ws/message and /_fenders/ws/disconnect, with the connection's id in the fenders-connection header; the app's executions send to a connection with POST http://fenders.internal/v1/run/ws/ID, close it with DELETE, and list the open ones with GET http://fenders.internal/v1/run/ws.

scale.description: How many executions serve the app's HTTP requests: at least min (none while idle when 0), more under load up to max.

expected_revision.description: The app's revision, as GET of the app gives it. It advances with every change to the app.
The app's revision, as GET of the app gives it. It advances with every change to the app.
The app's revision, as GET of the app gives it. It advances with every change to the app.
The triggers' own revision, as GET …/triggers gives it: not the app's.
The app's revision, as GET of the app gives it. It advances with every change to the app.

trigger_time.description: source=test-schedule only: one of the schedule's own times, recorded in the last 30 days or one of the next five. The command receives it as FENDERS_TRIGGER_TIME. Defaults to the submission time.

HttpSample.description: One request to make of the app through the gateway. An empty object asks for GET /.

path.description: Origin form: it starts with one slash and has no fragment.

body.description: At most 64 KiB; none for GET and HEAD.

HttpSampleResult.description: What became of a sample request. outcome is response when the app answered, refused when the gateway did not hand it to the app, and unconfirmed when it was handed over and no answer came back.

body.description: outcome=response: the first 16 KiB of the body, base64.

body_bytes.description: outcome=response: how much of the body was read, at most 1 MiB.

truncated.description: outcome=response: whether body is less than the app sent.

gateway_status.description: outcome=refused or unconfirmed: the status a client of the app would have been given.

Allowance.description: What a workspace may use. Always given whole.

cpu_percent.description: CPU its runs may hold at once, in hundredths of a core.

transfer_bytes.description: Outbound and gateway transfer in a UTC month.

WorkspaceUpdate.description: At least one of the two.

expected_revision.description: The workspace's allowance_revision, as GET /workspaces gives it to the operator. Not required; given, a change decided on an allowance that has changed since is 409.

name.description: A label. Two workspaces may share one; the id is what identifies.

lifecycle_revision.description: The operator's alone: what POST …/lifecycle expects.

Workspace.description: A workspace: what it is called, what it may use and how it stands. The revisions and the reason of a suspension are shown to the operator alone.

HttpLimits.description: How many requests of a workspace's HTTP apps may be in flight at once, and how many admitted in a minute.

expected_revision.description: The workspace's lifecycle_revision, as GET /workspaces gives it to the operator.

status.description: suspending until the workspace's executions have ended.

permissions.description: projects:write is not given to a key of one project.

label.description: One line the issuer wants recorded with what the key does. Not interpreted.

prefix.description: The start of the token, to tell keys apart by.
The start of the token, to tell keys apart by.

anyOf.description: Shown once and not kept. null when replayed.

replayed.description: true for a retry: nothing was issued, and no token can be shown. If the first answer was lost, revoke the key by its id and issue another.

cert_sha256.description: The pin of the node's certificate.
The pin of the node's certificate.

Node.description: A node: what it was registered with, what the operator set, and what it was last seen to be.

NodeMode.description: At least one. What is not named is left as it is.

NodeModeResult.description: What was asked, with the node's id.

anyOf.description: The digest of the policy this control plane was started with, or null when it has none.

pending_executions.description: Executions with public HTTPS access still to be stopped.

EgressPolicy.description: Whether apps may be given public HTTPS origins, and under which policy.

expected_revision.description: The policy's revision, as GET gives it.

ControlPlaneStatus.description: How this control plane's own loops are doing. A loop that runs is not proof that work is placed.

Me.description: The credential a request was made with: the operator's, or a key with its workspace, project, permissions and label.

workspace_id.description: The key's workspace; null for the operator.

Project.description: A project of a workspace. name is the name as it was given; slug is made of it, in lower case with hyphens, and is what must differ between a workspace's projects.

Usage.description: What a workspace or a project holds and has used, as of as_of.

UsageHistory.description: A page of a workspace's or a project's months. next is the cursor to pass as before.

next.description: The cursor to the page after this one: pass it as before. null when this is the last.

AppSizes.description: The sizes an app may take.

HttpsAccess.description: Whether apps of this project may be given public HTTPS origins.

HttpsValidated.description: The origins as they would be stored.

SchedulePreview.description: The next times a schedule would run.

Artifact.description: An uploaded component. The same bytes uploaded again to a project are the same artifact.

Inspection.description: What a node found of an artifact. state is valid once it may be deployed.

Connection.description: An HTTPS origin or a TCP endpoint apps of the project may be connected to. One that was revoked stays, with deleted true.

origin.description: type=https: the origin, with its port.

host.description: type=tcp: the host as it was given.

address.description: type=tcp: the address the host was resolved to, which is what a run may reach.

App.description: An app: its code, release, triggers and what it is doing.

revision.description: What a change to the app names as expected_revision.

AppPage.description: A page of App records. next is the cursor for the page after it, or null.

next.description: The cursor to the page after this one: pass it as before. null when this is the last.

ReleasePage.description: A page of Release records. next is the cursor for the page after it, or null.

next.description: The cursor to the page after this one: pass it as before. null when this is the last.

Run.description: One invocation of an app: manual, scheduled, or a recorded HTTP request.

RunPage.description: A page of Run records. next is the cursor for the page after it, or null.

next.description: The cursor to the page after this one: pass it as before. null when this is the last.

revision.description: What a change to the triggers names as expected_revision. It is the triggers' own, not the app's.
The app's revision: what a change to its connections names as expected_revision.

AppHttp.description: How an app's HTTP serving stands.

AppWebSocket.description: Whether an app accepts WebSocket connections, and those the gateway holds for it now.

path.description: The path its client asked for.

Event.description: A run or a lifecycle change of an app, with the transitions recorded of it.

EventPage.description: A page of Event records. next is the cursor for the page after it, or null.

next.description: The cursor to the page after this one: pass it as before. null when this is the last.

LogRecord.description: A piece of a run's output. bytes is base64, with the values of the run's secrets masked.

id.description: The execution's id and the record's sequence.

gap_from.description: Set where output before this record was lost.

LogPage.description: A page of a run's output, oldest first. Unlike other lists it is read forwards, with after.

has_more.description: Whether more is already there to read.

next.description: Where this page ends: pass it as after to read on, now or later. Always given, because output is read forwards and more may come.

Diagnostic.description: What an outcome means: code to branch on, and a summary and a detail in words, whose wording may change. Present where there is something to say. It does not say where to look or whom to ask: that is for the product built on this API.

code.description: The reason, or unrecognized. Codes may be added.
